method: Canonical IDs are exact Glottocodes; unknown samples and internal study clades retain source-specific IDs. Original sample labels remain on source-tagged edges. Tree hypotheses are never combined across sources as one asserted ancestry. Incompatibility is computed only between rooted summary topologies restricted to at least three shared, non-repeated, non-ancestor tip IDs. Sample absence and polytomies alone are not classified as conflict. Source-specific summary trees, not posterior samples, are imported.
catalogDiscovery: All 30 data repositories returned by the Phlorest organization repository search on 2026-10-12, excluding phlorest software and .github; second page empty.

debates.title: Transeurasian relationship
debates.status: Disputed genealogical proposal; no consensus implied

positions.author: Robbeets et al. (2021)
positions.claim: Under the Transeurasian hypothesis, Japonic, Koreanic, Tungusic, Mongolic and Turkic are branches of one proposed genealogical group.

positions.author: Tian et al. (2022)
positions.claim: This critique argues that the linguistic, genetic and archaeological analyses do not provide conclusive evidence for that family or its proposed farming dispersal. This is rejection of the evidence, not a demonstrated alternative superfamily.

positions.author: Robbeets et al. (2022)
positions.claim: The response revises datasets and approaches while defending the proposed relationship and the triangulation argument.

debates.note: This is a manually curated paper-level debate. Its full proposed topology has not been imported; the five family labels are not a reconstruction of its internal branching.
